text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Top: the forecasts are re-fitted on a synthetic target in which measured power is cut by 2%, 5%, or 10%, in 9 of the 18 scored months (chosen at random with a fixed seed) and in a random half of the other months. A lag that worked would gain more the bigger the cut. Change in error, L1 minus B0, in percentage points of capacity; more negative is better. Interval: 99%, as for the planned contrasts. The oracle (B0 given the true shift factor) gains 0.39 points at 10%. Bottom: the change in error from L1 compared with two random-day lags, and from a random-day lag compared with B0 (the change from adding any extra column). Interval: 95%, as for every exploratory contrast.'

text.aria-label: Title text 'Dot: estimate. Line: confidence interval from resampling whole months. Zero: no change. Months being scored are the months the fitted forecasts are tested on. All rows are exploratory. Oracle rows are post hoc, from round 1's rebuilt month-level control; L1 rows are the first run's. Arms. B0: the XGBoost baseline with no lagged power. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). N1: a random day 8 to 28 days earlier (keeps the plant's slowly changing output level). N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control).'
text.tspan: Dot: estimate. Line: confidence interval from resampling whole months. Zero: no change. Months being scored are the months
the fitted forecasts are tested on.
Oracle rows are post hoc, from round 1's rebuilt month-level control; L1 rows are the first run's.
Arms. B0: the XGBoost baseline with no lagged power. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before
the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). N1: a random day 8 to 28 days earlier
(keeps the plant's slowly changing output level). N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control).
